relevance_note: Broecker et al., what verification of AI-based forecasting systems needs — methodological guardrails for your own evaluation.

title: Uncertainty quantification for data-driven weather models
relevance_note: Systematic comparison of UQ routes for a deterministic AI model (Pangu): initial-condition ensembles vs statistical/ML post-hoc UQ, over Europe.

venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: RainScaleGAN, conditional GAN for rainfall downscaling.

relevance_note: Conditional diffusion performing bias correction and downscaling jointly, trained on observations only via a shared embedding space. Relevant because the user has only station observations as truth.

title: Numerical models outperform AI weather forecasts of record-breaking extremes
relevance_note: Preprint of the above with the fuller quantitative statement.

title: Forecasting the Future With Yesterday's Climate: Temperature Bias in AI Weather and Climate Models
relevance_note: Landsberg et al.: AI models are COLD-BIASED, resembling climates 15-20 yr earlier than the predicted period; cold bias strongest at hottest temperatures. A trained-on-history artefact your bias correction would inherit.

title: Self-Attentive Transformer for Fast and Accurate Postprocessing of Temperature and Wind Speed Forecasts
venue: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
relevance_note: Transformer postprocessing all lead times jointly on EUPPBench; 16.5% CRPS gain for 2m temperature over raw, beating member-by-member benchmark.

title: Probabilistic measures afford fair comparisons of AIWP and NWP model output
relevance_note: Potential CRPS: fair comparison of AI and physical models by subjecting both to the same IDR postprocessing. The correct way to frame 'is AIFS better here'.

title: Probabilistic Temperature Forecasting with a Heteroscedastic Autoregressive Ensemble Postprocessing model
venue: Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society
relevance_note: Heteroscedastic autoregressive EMOS for temperature: explicit treatment of error autocorrelation in time.

title: Super-resolving coarse-resolution weather forecasts with flow matching
relevance_note: Delefosse et al.: generative super-resolution as a POST-PROCESSING step decoupled from forecasting; re-coarsening consistency check + spectral diagnostics. A clean methodological template.

title: Joint bias correction and downscaling of subseasonal forecasts via diffusion models
relevance_note: Pyrina et al.: joint bias correction and downscaling of subseasonal forecasts via diffusion.

title: Efficient Kilometer‐Scale Precipitation Downscaling With Conditional Wavelet Diffusion
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation
relevance_note: Wavelet-domain conditional diffusion achieving 10x precipitation super-resolution to 1 km with a reported 9x inference speedup over pixel-space diffusion. Read for the efficiency trick if diffusion is attempted on limited hardware.

title: Intelligent Shanghai Typhoon Model (ISTM): A Diffusion‐Based Downscaling Emulator From AIFS to Kilometer‐Scale Regional Reanalysis for Typhoon Forecasts
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation
relevance_note: ISTM: diffusion downscaling emulator from AIFS to km-scale regional reanalysis; cuts 72-h typhoon intensity error ~39.5% vs AIFS. Proof that AIFS-to-km-scale generative downscaling works.

title: Spatial postprocessing of ensemble forecasts for temperature using nonhomogeneous Gaussian regression
relevance_note: Spatial extension of NGR for temperature with locally adaptive climatology; Gaussian random field vs ECC for spatial dependence.

title: SEEPS4ALL: an open dataset for the verification of daily precipitation forecasts using station climate statistics
relevance_note: SEEPS4ALL: open dataset for verifying daily precipitation forecasts using station data — relevant given ISD-Lite precip is empty.

title: Area-covering postprocessing of ensemble precipitation forecasts using topographical and seasonal conditions
relevance_note: Area-covering EMOS using topographical and seasonal predictors instead of station identity - how to postprocess where there is no station.

title: Seamless multi-model postprocessing for air temperature forecasts in complex topography
relevance_note: Multi-model EMOS blending a convection-permitting LAM with a global ensemble for temperature at Swiss stations; 30% over high-res DMO, 8-12% over single-model EMOS; worst in winter.

title: Convolutional conditional neural processes for local climate downscaling
relevance_note: convCNP downscaling: trained model predicts at ARBITRARY locations including stations with no training data. The 'unseen station' architecture.

title: Graph Neural Networks and Spatial Information Learning for Post-Processing Ensemble Weather Forecasts
relevance_note: GNN postprocessing: stations as graph nodes with attention over neighbours; substantial gain over a strong DRN baseline for 2m temperature over Europe.

title: Gradient-Boosted Mixture Regression Models for Postprocessing Ensemble Weather Forecasts
relevance_note: MIXSAMOS-GB: gradient-boosted MIXTURE regression on standardized anomalies; outperforms state-of-the-art postprocessing for German 2m temperature. Pooled-training + boosting, no deep learning.

title: Earth observation embeddings are effective sub-grid descriptors for probabilistic weather downscaling
relevance_note: Earth-observation foundation-model embeddings as learned sub-grid surface descriptors; +11.5% CRPS for 2m temperature at stations held out in SPACE and time, and works with AI-model input.

title: Generative Modeling of High-resolution Global Precipitation Forecasts
relevance_note: Generative modelling of high-resolution global precipitation forecasts. Preprint; companion to CorrectorGAN.

title: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution Model for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
relevance_note: Pangu preprint; more architecture detail on 3DEST and the greedy multi-timestep scheme.

title: Residual Corrective Diffusion Modeling for Km-scale Atmospheric Downscaling
relevance_note: CorrDiff preprint version (journal version doi:10.1038/s43247-025-02042-5). Cite the journal version; preprint listed for completeness.

title: Precipitation Downscaling with Spatiotemporal Video Diffusion
relevance_note: Spatiotemporal video diffusion for precipitation super-resolution with a deterministic downscaler followed by a temporally conditioned diffusion stage, compared against six baselines on FV3GFS. Preprint; argues explicitly that the conditional distribution, not the mean, is what matters.

title: Emerging AI-based weather prediction models as downscaling tools
relevance_note: Uses existing AI-NWP models themselves as downscaling operators, initialised from smoothed ERA5 and coarse CMIP6 fields at one-day lead, for 2-m temperature. An unusual and cheap alternative framing. Preprint.

title: Regional data-driven weather modeling with a global stretched-grid
relevance_note: Nipen et al.: STRETCHED-GRID extension of AIFS itself — 2.5 km over the Nordics, 31 km globally; pre-trained on 43 yr ERA5 then refined on 3.3 yr MEPS analyses; beats MEPS control and ensemble mean for 2 m temperature. The most directly transferable design for NW Russia.

title: Efficient Localized Adaptation of Neural Weather Forecasting: A Case Study in the MENA Region
relevance_note: Localised adaptation of a neural weather model for a specific region (MENA). Preprint; the fine-tuning-a-global-model-for-one-region pattern, which is the compute-feasible route.

title: TAUDiff: Highly efficient kilometer-scale downscaling using generative diffusion models
relevance_note: TAUDiff: names spectral bias in deterministic regression downscaling as the problem and pairs a deterministic mean-field model with a SMALLER generative diffusion model for the fine-scale residual, for wind velocity. Preprint; the efficiency-minded version of corrective diffusion.

title: Fixing the Double Penalty in Data-Driven Weather Forecasting Through a Modified Spherical Harmonic Loss Function
relevance_note: Shows that the MSE loss used by most data-driven forecast models causes double-penalty smoothing, and that a parameter-free spherical-harmonic loss modification, applied by FINE-TUNING GraphCast, raised effective resolution from 1250 km to 160 km with better ensemble spread and better surface wind extremes. The cleanest quantification of MSE-induced smoothing, and a fine-tuning-scale intervention.

title: Building Machine Learning Limited Area Models: Kilometer-Scale Weather Forecasting in Realistic Settings
relevance_note: Adamov et al.: kilometre-scale ML limited-area models with flexible boundary forcing; systematic ablation of boundary width and graph construction; verified against stations.

title: A comparison of stretched-grid and limited-area modelling for data-driven regional weather forecasting
relevance_note: Wijnands et al.: head-to-head of stretched-grid vs limited-area for regional data-driven forecasting over Europe; SGM is self-contained and generalises better temporally.

title: CRPS-LAM: Probabilistic Regional Weather Forecasting with Continuous Ranked Probability Score
relevance_note: CRPS-LAM: hybrid CNN/GNN regional ensemble model trained on a CRPS objective, generating members in a single forward pass with roughly 39x speedup over diffusion baselines. Preprint; the compute-efficient alternative to diffusion for probabilistic regional output.

title: Assessing the Geographic Generalization and Physical Consistency of Generative Models for Climate Downscaling
relevance_note: CRITICAL NEGATIVE RESULT. Benchmarks generative downscaling models with physics-inspired diagnostics and finds that CorrDiff-class models trained on central Europe fail to generalise to Iberia, Morocco or SCANDINAVIA, and fail to reproduce derived second-order fields such as divergence and vorticity. Preprint; the strongest published warning against importing a pretrained generative downscaler into northwest Russia.

title: High-Resolution Probabilistic Data-Driven Weather Modeling with a Stretched-Grid
relevance_note: Nordhagen et al.: probabilistic stretched-grid Nordic model, CRPS-trained in grid-point AND SPECTRAL space. Spectral loss term is NECESSARY for spatially coherent fields; -13% CRPS on 2 m T and -10% on MSLP vs MEPS. Read for the loss-function lesson.

title: On Global Applicability and Location Transferability of Generative Deep Learning Models for Precipitation Downscaling
relevance_note: Systematic assessment of generative precipitation-downscaling generalisation across 15 world regions using a hierarchical location-based split, with ERA5 predictors and IMERG 0.1 deg targets. Preprint; the companion transferability study.

title: STIPP: Space-time in situ postprocessing over the French Alps using proper scoring rules
relevance_note: STIPP: space-time in-situ postprocessing at STATION locations using proper scoring rules; makes hourly ensembles from a 6-hourly deterministic forecast. Closest method template to your station-level task.

title: AI-Based Regional Emulation for Kilometer-Scale Dynamical Downscaling
relevance_note: AI limited-area emulator trained on ERA5 0.25 deg 3-hourly forcings against 4 km hourly CONUS404, generalising to a 1.0 deg non-ERA5 forcing. Preprint; shows what a full AI dynamical-downscaling emulator costs and requires.

title: From AI Weather Prediction to Infrastructure Resilience: A Real-Time Correction-Downscaling Framework for Tropical Cyclone Impact Forecasting
relevance_note: Real-time correction-plus-downscaling of AI forecasts to 500 m wind fields for typhoon impact, reporting a 38.8% reduction in station-scale wind-speed MAE relative to Pangu-Weather and roughly 25 s per 12-h cycle on a SINGLE GPU. The clearest evidence that a correct-then-downscale pipeline is feasible on modest hardware. Preprint 2026.

title: AIFS-COMPO: A Global Data-Driven Atmospheric Composition Forecasting System
relevance_note: AIFS-COMPO atmospheric composition — evidence of the modular Anemoi/AIFS ecosystem you could build on.

authors: Joffrey Dumont Le Brazidec et al.
title: Downscaling weather forecasts from Low- to High-Resolution with Diffusion Models
relevance_note: Dumont Le Brazidec et al.: diffusion downscaling of IFS ensembles 100 km -> 30 km via residual learning; reproduces target power spectra at small scales, physically consistent wind-pressure coupling.

title: Enhancing AI and Dynamical Subseasonal Forecasts with Probabilistic Bias Correction
relevance_note: Probabilistic bias correction applied to ECMWF's leading dynamical and AI models, reported to double AIFS subseasonal skill. Preprint 2026; relevant as the pure-postprocessing upper bound.

title: Representing the Surface Ocean in ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system AIFS
relevance_note: AIFS ocean/wave/sea-ice coupling — matters for the Baltic/Barents/White Sea part of your box.

title: Extreme Weather Bench: A framework and benchmark for evaluation of high-impact weather
relevance_note: Extreme Weather Bench: community benchmark for high-impact weather; the verification framework to adopt rather than invent.

title: AIFS-DOP: End-to-End Medium-Range Weather Prediction from Observations Alone with Machine Learning
relevance_note: AIFS-DOP: trained on gridded OBSERVATIONS alone, no reanalysis — directly relevant to your finding that ERA5 assimilates your stations.

title: Towards Fair Comparisons of AI- and Physics-Based Weather Models for Extreme Events via the Weighted Potential CRPS
relevance_note: Weighted potential CRPS for fair comparison of AI and physics-based models on extreme events; the current frontier of this argument.

title: AIFS-SUBS: Extending Data-Driven Forecasting to Sub-Seasonal Timescales
relevance_note: AIFS-SUBS: sub-seasonal AIFS, weeks 2-6, ~200x less inference energy than IFS. Shows the AIFS family is expanding into your lead-time range.

title: HourGlass: A probabilistic data-driven temporal downscaler for global and regional weather forecasting
relevance_note: HourGlass: probabilistic TEMPORAL downscaler applied to AIFS-Single and AIFS-ENS (and MET Norway's Bris). Notes deterministic temporal downscaling produces overly smooth fields.

title: GraphCast Skill and Systematic Biases in Indian Summer Monsoon Forecasts: Evaluation Against ERA5 and IMERG
relevance_note: GraphCast Indian monsoon evaluation: regional power-spectrum variance ratio 0.14 vs IMERG, compressed rainfall intensity distribution — a clean quantification of deterministic smoothing.

title: Do AI weather models miss extremes?
relevance_note: Gabler et al., station-based (not reanalysis-based) extremes verification of 11 systems over Europe, 10 months. AIFS loses 4.9+/-2.0% in the heat tail; ALL models incl. NWP show a shared conditional bias toward the distribution centre. The single most relevant error-mode paper for station-based work.

authors: Simon Lang; Mihai Alexe; Matthew Chantry; Jesper Dramsch; Florian Pinault; Baudouin Raoult et al.
title: AIFS -- ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system
relevance_note: AIFS - ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system. GNN encoder/decoder with sliding-window transformer processor, trained on ERA5 and ECMWF operational NWP analyses. Read first: this is the base model.

authors: Nikolay Koldunov; Thomas Rackow; Christian Lessig; Sergey Danilov; Suvarchal K. Cheedela; Dmitry Sidorenko et al.
title: Emerging AI-based weather prediction models as downscaling tools
relevance_note: Koldunov et al.: emerging AI-based weather prediction models AS DOWNSCALING TOOLS. The single most directly on-brief preprint - proposes using existing AI-NWP systems for downscaling rather than training from scratch.

authors: Muhammad Akhtar Munir; Fahad Shahbaz Khan; Salman Khan
title: Efficient Localized Adaptation of Neural Weather Forecasting: A Case Study in the MENA Region
relevance_note: Munir et al.: efficient LOCALIZED ADAPTATION of neural weather forecasting (MENA case study). Fine-tuning a global neural forecast to one region - the compute-feasible pattern for a 4 GB GPU.

authors: Simon Lang; Mihai Alexe; Mariana C. A. Clare; Christopher Roberts; Rilwan Adewoyin; Zied Ben Bouallègue et al.
title: AIFS-CRPS: Ensemble forecasting using a model trained with a loss function based on the Continuous Ranked Probability Score
relevance_note: AIFS-CRPS: ensemble variant trained directly on a CRPS-based loss. Relevant because the archive available is the 51-member AIFS ENS.

authors: Jasper S. Wijnands; Michiel Van Ginderachter; Bastien François; Sophie Buurman; Piet Termonia; Dieter Van den Bleeken
title: A comparison of stretched-grid and limited-area modelling for data-driven regional weather forecasting
relevance_note: Wijnands et al.: stretched-grid vs limited-area data-driven regional forecasting with GNNs. The two architectural options for a regional AI model, and their boundary-condition trade-offs.

authors: Gabriel Moldovan; Ewan Pinnington; Ana Prieto Nemesio; Simon Lang; Zied Ben Bouallègue; Jesper Dramsch et al.
title: An update to ECMWF's machine-learned weather forecast model AIFS
relevance_note: Update to AIFS Single: physical-consistency bounding layers substantially improve PRECIPITATION forecasts, plus expanded variable set. Matters given precipitation is the unverifiable variable locally.
